passage:
In Oslo, Emil's first six months looked good on paper. The job was what he had hoped for, the salary was fair and the project was growing. One Sunday in March, he took out his original list of what mattered and read it slowly.
Career: check. Money: check. Then the third line: people. His phone showed no messages from anyone in the city, and the flat was quiet.
He told his colleague Felix, "I never thought the evenings would be so long." Felix grinned. "There's a running club on Tuesdays. Come."
Emil went, and on Wednesday he arranged a weekly video call with his parents for Sundays. Ten weeks later he had two people to text about the weekend, and the evenings felt shorter.

qa.q: On which day is the running club?
qa.a: The running club meets on Tuesdays.

qa.q: What was Emil feeling when he read the third line of the list?
qa.a: Emil felt lonely and quietly disappointed, since the flat was quiet and no messages from the city came.

qa.q: What could Emil do if the running club does not lead to friendships?
qa.a: Emil could try another group, such as a language or board game evening, and keep the weekly call home.

qa.q: How might Felix have felt hearing Emil say the evenings were long?
qa.a: Felix probably felt friendly concern and wanted to help, so invited Emil to the running club.

grounding: The passage shows a person checking an overseas move against original values after six months, finding community missing, and joining local groups and setting weekly calls home.

At his six-month check-in, in the small meeting room on the ninth floor of the Toronto office, Shankar surprised his mentor, Kiran, by taking out a folded page. 'I wrote this before I moved. My reasons.' Three lines: grow as a data engineer; save for my parents' house repairs; have people around me.
Kiran read it. 'And?'
'The first two, yes. I lead a small project now, and I'm saving. The third, no. I go from office to flat. Weekends are laundry and calls.'
He had already done something about it, he said. He had signed up for a Sunday volunteering slot at the community centre near his flat, joined the office cricket group and fixed video calls home every Wednesday and Saturday. 'It's not a failure,' Kiran said. 'It's a check.'

qa.q: What were the three lines on Shankar's page?
qa.a: Grow as a data engineer; save for my parents' house repairs; have people around me.

qa.q: How does Shankar feel about the third line?
qa.a: He seems lonely and a bit disappointed that weekends are only laundry and calls, even though work and saving are going well.

qa.q: What could Shankar do at the next check-in?
qa.a: He could bring the same page back in six months to see whether the volunteering and the cricket group have filled the gap.

qa.q: How does Kiran see Shankar's review?
qa.a: Kiran sees it as a healthy check rather than a failure, and seems encouraged that Shankar already acted.

grounding: It shows someone six months after moving checking against the original values, finding community missing, and joining local groups and setting regular calls home.

Hi Zainab,
Six months in Berlin today, so I did the thing you made me promise: I reopened the list I wrote before leaving. 1. A research job in my field. 2. Money to help with Abba's loan. 3. A life that isn't only work.
Honest check: 1, yes, the lab is everything I hoped. 2, yes, slowly. 3, no. I realised I haven't had a proper conversation with anyone outside the lab since March. Weekends I sleep and scroll.
So this week I joined a Sunday choir at the community hall, even though I can't sing, and a Wednesday language café. I've also fixed Friday evening calls with Ammi and Abba, no cancelling.
I'll tell you if the choir survives me.
Ankita

qa.q: What did Ankita join at the community hall?
How does Ankita feel about the third line on the list?
qa.a: Ankita feels lonely and a little uneasy, noticing no proper conversation outside the lab since March.

qa.q: What else could help Ankita if the choir doesn't work out?
qa.a: Ankita could try another group built around an interest, such as hiking or books, and keep reviewing the list every six months.

qa.q: How might Ammi and Abba be affected by the fixed Friday calls?
qa.a: They get a dependable time to hear from Ankita, which likely eases their worry and makes the distance feel smaller.

grounding: It shows someone six months after migrating checking against the original values, finding community missing and joining local groups and scheduling calls home.
